source: Spiridonov, Erofeeva, Klowait, Morozov, Ardislamov (2026) The modulating role of sources of difficulty in interactive matchstick algebra
finding: Conceptual extended replication of the interactivity effect on Knoblich-type matchstick problems. Interactive conditions did not raise success. Movement did not help chunk decomposition and hurt relaxation of high-level constraints.
numbers: Exp 1 N=105 (108 recruited): interactive assembled sticks (N=54) solved problems A/B/C/D at 0.91/0.87/0.59/0.67 vs static sticks (N=51) 0.94/0.80/0.59/0.69. Exp 2 N=88 (groups of 20-24): problem C solved 0.52 interactive sticks, 0.35 static sticks, 0.52 static paper, 0.63 interactive assembled. Exp 3 VR N=73. Problems B and C (constraint problems) showed lower success with more movements.
quote: we hypothesized that the influence of interactivity would vary based on the specific sources of difficulty
limits: This tests the interactivity add-on (Vallee-Tourangeau), not the core 1999 ordering of constraint difficulty. The paper still uses Knoblich's A<B<C frame. Student samples, mean age about 19.7, about 80% female.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: no failed replication of the core constraint-relaxation ordering was found. The one replication failure is for the physical-interaction add-on. Do not assume acting on the problem always helps restructuring.

source: Web search snippets (Collier and Beeman; compound RAT incubation; Valueva 2024; one quasi-experimental RAT study)
finding: Snippets only: a delayed-incubation effect on compound RAT appears in some studies, with more insight reports after incubation. One quasi-experimental RAT study found no incubation effect.
numbers: Snippet quotes a mean d of about .32 over 117 studies (same meta-analysis as Sio and Ormerod, recorded as 0.29 weighted / 0.41 unweighted in a04). No new N read.
limits: Not opened. Numbers are search snippets. Treat as a pointer to the null RAT study only.
agent_relevance: Incubation on RAT items is real but not guaranteed. Any agent incubation test needs a no-break control and should expect a small effect.

source: Negative search: LLM incubation, context reset or parked subproblem on RAT or compound RAT items
finding: No LLM study of incubation, context reset or parked subproblem on RAT items was found with WebSearch. arXiv API returned empty, OpenAlex hit its free-budget limit, Semantic Scholar returned 429.
limits: Absence of evidence under tool limits.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 stays open. Nearest indirect evidence is sequential vs parallel scaling (d04).

source: Mirtaheri, Edelman, Jelassi, Malach, Boix-Adsera (2025) Let Me Think! A Long Chain-of-Thought Can Be Worth Exponentially Many Short Ones
finding: On hard graph-connectivity distributions, one long sequential chain beats aggregating many short chains, provably and in experiments on trained transformers and large reasoning models.
numbers: Theory: one polynomial-length chain solves it while polynomially many constant-length chains cannot. Table values not extracted.
limits: Graph connectivity only. Only the abstract and introduction were read. Sequential cost grows with context length.
agent_relevance: Context reset or restart is not free. Where state must be carried forward, fresh parallel tries lose. Use context-drop restart (O6) only when the old context is the fixation, not when it holds needed state.

source: Zhao et al. (2026) TrigReason: Trigger-Based Collaboration between Small and Large Reasoning Models
finding: Stall detectors in practice: hesitation phrases, loops and token overconfidence (perplexity ratio) trigger a large-model intervention. It is an efficiency paper, not an accuracy-at-equal-tokens test of restructuring.
numbers: Matches full-LRM accuracy on AIME24, AIME25, GPQA-D while offloading 1.70x-4.79x more steps to the small model. Latency -43.9%, API cost -73.3%. Table 2 (AIME24): total trigger rate 50.92% of steps gives 30.0% accuracy, 25.08% gives 26.25%; switching off the loop-intervention trigger (4.87% to 0) gives 23.33 vs about 27 to 30. Overconfident steps (>85% confidence) are 38.1% of small-model steps.
limits: QwQ-32B plus small models. AIME24 has 30 problems, so differences of a few points are one or two problems. Detector precision and recall as an impasse classifier are not reported.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: loop and hesitation triggers carry measurable value, but no head-to-head of detectors as impasse classifiers exists. Cheap lexical and loop detectors are usable first-line S6 signals.

source: Wang, McInerney, Wang, Kallus (2026) EAT: Entropy After </Think> for reasoning model early exiting
finding: A one-token entropy signal (entropy of the next token after an appended stop-thinking token) stabilizes when Pass@1 plateaus. A variance-on-moving-average rule stops reasoning early. Models often settle on the right answer in the first 10-20% of the budget and keep revising.
numbers: Token use cut 12-22% (up to 21% on AIME-2025) on MATH-500 and AIME-2025 with no accuracy loss. Works with proxy models (1.5B proxy for Llama 70B, local 4B for Claude 3.7).
limits: Tested as a stop signal, not as a restructure trigger. Gains smaller on newer Qwen3-8B. Needs logits or a proxy model.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: an entropy signal is validated for 'enough thinking, stop'. The same signal staying flat and high is a plausible S6 stall flag, untested for restructuring.

source: Guan et al. (2026) Mitigating Overthinking in Large Reasoning Language Models via Reasoning Path Deviation Monitoring
finding: Overthinking trajectories drift off the correct path and show frequent high-entropy transition tokens. A path-deviation index of these tokens triggers early exit without a proxy model.
numbers: Authors claim the largest gain over vanilla CoT among early-exit methods (abstract and intro read; per-benchmark numbers not extracted).
limits: Only abstract and introduction read. Early exit, not restart.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: supports high-entropy transition tokens as a deviation signal, a candidate S6 trigger next to EAT.

source: NeuReasoner (arXiv 2604.02972) stagnation flag, from search snippet
finding: Snippet: a trace is marked stagnant when strategy oscillation or repetitive checks occur and information entropy is not decreasing.
numbers: No numbers read. PDF fetch timed out.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: another vote for 'repetition plus non-falling uncertainty' as the stall rule. Verify before relying on it.

source: Haq, Chhaya, Pandey, Bhattacharya (2025) Is your LLM trapped in a Mental Set?
finding: Einstellung-style test on math equivalence (DeCaro 2016 problems): does solving complex problems first make models miss shortcuts. Effects are inconsistent and the sample is tiny.
numbers: 6 problems per type per condition. Few-shot exact match: GPT-4o shortcut alone 0.33, shortcut after complex 0.66; complex alone 0.66, complex after shortcut 0.83. Llama-70B shortcut 0 then 0.16. Llama-8B shortcut 0.16 then 0. With zero-shot CoT added: GPT-4o 0.66/0.66 and 0.83/0.83. CoT models take about 3 steps where humans use 1.
limits: Prior complex problems helped GPT-4o, the opposite of classic Einstellung. Each cell is 6 items, so 0.16 is one problem. Not frontier reasoning models.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: no clean carried-over fixation penalty on these models. Measured LLM fixation is about in-context red herrings (Only Connect, c08), not carried-over strategy.

source: Naeini et al. (2023) LLMs are Fixated by Red Herrings: Only Connect Wall
finding: Downloaded but numbers were not re-extracted this session. Used as already recorded in evidence_c (c08). No post-2025 test of the red-herring penalty on frontier reasoning models was found.
limits: GPT-3.5/4 era models. Frontier reasoning models untested in the located literature.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 stays open: size of the fixation penalty on frontier reasoning models is unmeasured. Run our own test.

source: Lu, Teehan, Jin, Ren (2026) When Does Verification Pay Off? A Closer Look at LLMs as Solution Verifiers
finding: Across 37 models and 9 benchmarks, cross-family verification gives more gain than same-family or self-verification. Self-verification gives the smallest verifier gain and reasoning post-training weakens it.
numbers: Spontaneous self-verification keywords appear in 96% of Qwen3 and 73% of DeepSeek outputs vs 1-2% for Llama3 and Qwen2.5. False-positive rate rises in self- and intra-family verification. Math and logic tasks give the highest gains.
limits: Rejection-sampling gain metric, not equal-token controlled. Tasks are not insight riddles.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: an independent verifier from another model family is the best-supported fix for S8 when a model accepts its own wrong answer or rejects its own right one. A same-model second pass is weak.

source: Singhi et al. (2025) When To Solve, When To Verify: Compute-Optimal Problem Solving and Generative Verification (COLM 2025)
finding: At fixed inference budget, self-consistency (more solutions) beats generative verification at low and moderate budgets.
numbers: Generative verification first matches self-consistency after about 8x compute and needs about 128x more compute for a 3.8% gain. Holds for Llama and Qwen 7B-70B and QwQ-32B on math.
limits: Math only. The verifier is a trained or prompted generative reward model, not an insight check.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 equal-token answer: at small budgets spend tokens on more independent attempts. Add a verifier only at larger budgets, and keep S8 checks cheap.

source: Tan et al. (2025) Too Consistent to Detect: A Study of Self-Consistent Errors in LLMs
finding: Errors repeated across samples (self-consistent) do not shrink with model size and evade consistency, probability and probe detectors. A cross-model probe from an external verifier LLM helps.
numbers: Inconsistent-error detection reaches AUROC up to about 90%; all four detector families drop sharply on self-consistent errors. Cross-model probe improves on three LLM families (exact gains not extracted).
limits: Factual QA (SciQ, TriviaQA), not insight tasks. Tables only partly read.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 and 5: repeated-answer rate is a poor impasse or correctness signal when the model is confidently wrong (a false insight). Use an external or different-model check.

source: Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models (arXiv 2601.00514), re-use for Gap 6
finding: Already recorded in a21 and b01: spontaneous Aha shifts in 6.31% of traces, pooled accuracy 6.6% with a shift vs 29.0% without. No study was located that correlates verbal confidence jumps with correctness at item level the way human Aha ratings are.
numbers: See a21. No new study located.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: LLM Aha shifts behave like false insights on average, not like the human Aha-accuracy link. Closed for trace shifts, open for verbal confidence jumps.

source: Ouyang et al. (2026) ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory (ICLR 2026)
finding: Distilling strategies from successes and failures into a retrievable memory improves later task success over memory-free agents and over raw-trajectory memories.
numbers: WebArena success +8.3, +7.2, +4.6 over memory-free agents across three backbones. Up to 20% relative gain and 16% fewer interaction steps vs baselines. Parallel test-time scaling (k=5) adds more.
limits: Web and SWE tasks, not insight items. No arm stores the restructuring step separately, so the human insight-memory advantage is not tested.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: storing condensed strategy (including from failures) helps reuse. Indirect support for logging O6 restructures.

source: Zhao et al. (2026) Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers
finding: Agents depend on raw experience but often ignore or misread condensed experience, even when it is the only experience provided.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: caution. A stored restructuring note must be checked for causal use. Store the raw example with the note and test with a perturbation control.

source: Replication search for the Alderete context-graph restructuring result
finding: Searched for replications of the context-graph gain (73.3% to 93.9%, n=30 vs 33). None found.
limits: Search limited by API rate limits this session.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 stays open. Keep that claim single-source.

source: Liu, Karimnazarov, White (2025) Trapped by Expectations: Functional Fixedness in LLM-Enabled Chat Search
finding: Functional fixedness here is in human users of chat search, not model fixation. 450 participants did six tasks. Unmet expectations led to more detailed prompts.
agent_relevance: Excluded from fixation evidence for the agent. Do not count it for Gap 3.
